changed.note: datetime.utcnow() -> datetime.now(timezone.utc). Credentials.__post_init__ normalizes expiration to naive UTC, so the stored value is wrapped with .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) before comparing against the aware now value.

utcnow = datetime.utcnow() -> datetime.now(timezone.utc); added timezone to the datetime import. The value flows only into get_credential_string, to_amz_date and post_presign_v4, which all go through time._to_utc and accept aware datetimes. No comparisons or arithmetic on it.

datetime.utcnow().replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) -> datetime.now(timezone.utc). The redundant .replace was dropped so tzinfo is set once. This branch only runs on Python without datetime.UTC (3.10); the 3.11+ branch already returned an aware value, so behavior there is unchanged.

guesses.assumed: Credentials.expiration is always naive UTC at this point, because __post_init__ strips tzinfo after converting to UTC and the dataclass is frozen. So .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) is a correct reinterpretation and not a change of the instant. Reviewer should confirm no code path sets expiration after construction.
Dropping the trailing .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) is equivalent, because datetime.now(timezone.utc) is already aware in UTC.
